classification.text_en: The hoopoe (al-hudhud) is one of the birds (al-tayr) among Sulayman's hosts.

origin.note_en: The Quran does not describe the creation of the hoopoe in particular.

purpose.note_en: The Quran does not state a purpose for the hoopoe.

nature.text_en: In the account the hoopoe speaks to Sulayman, says he has comprehended what Sulayman had not, and reports people prostrating to the sun instead of God.

abilities.text_en: He came with sure news from Saba and told of a woman ruling them with a great throne. Sulayman then told him to cast a letter to them and turn away from them.

limitations.note_en: The Quran does not describe limits of the hoopoe.

relationship_with_humans.text_en: Sulayman checked on the birds and noticed the hoopoe's absence. He warned of a severe punishment unless the hoopoe brought clear authority, then said they would see whether he spoke truth.

quranic_events.text_en: Sulayman missed the hoopoe, who stayed away for a short while and returned with news from Saba. Sulayman tested the report and sent a letter with him.

chronological_position.text_en: The event is in Sulayman's time. The passage gives no date.

location.text_en: He brought news from Saba and stayed away not far in distance.

misconceptions.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the passage tells the hoopoe's report and Sulayman's test of it. It does not say the bird was punished, so no punishment is claimed here.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the king weighs the report ('we will see whether you spoke truth') rather than accepting or dismissing it at once, which is read as a lesson in verifying news.

vocabulary.text_en: Words used: al-hudhud (the hoopoe), al-tayr (the birds), saba' (Saba), naba' yaqin (sure news), sultan mubin (clear authority).
